newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African gang robs 40 tourists in single attack.
newsitem.headline: S.African gang robs 40 tourists in single attack.

text.p: South African robbers armed with handguns held up at least 40 foreign tourists in a Johannesburg tourist hostel before escaping with money and jewellery last week, police said on Tuesday.

Police acknowledged on Tuesday that news of the robbery, which took place last Thursday at the Backpackers Ritz hostel in Johannesburg's upmarket Dunkeld West suburb, had been deliberately withheld because of its "sensitivity".
Sharma Maharaj, police chief for the Gauteng region, said in a statement that he had opened an inquiry and pledged that action would be taken against the officer responsible.
"I must repudiate outright the excuse that information was suppressed due to its 'sensitivity', or the fact that so many tourists were involved," Maharaj said.

"This is reminiscent of certain old apartheid practises... History has clearly shown that the wholesale suppression of information on events is totally counterproductive and can only undermine credibility, as in this case."
South African police have declared war on a wave of violent crime. Johannesburg has been particularly hard-hit and has been dubbed the "crime capital of the world" by local criminologists.
Tourists fleeced during the robbery were from Australia, Britain, France, Canada, America, Japan, Finland, New Zealand, Chile, Venezuela, Belgium, Denmark and Israel.

No one was hurt in the robbery that took place late at night but the six robbers escaped with cash and jewellery worth 50,000 rand ($11,061). Some of the tourists were also robbed of their passports and airplane tickets.
